description: Search the patristic corpus BY WRITER rather than by verse — the corpus is 62,484 passages from 314 writers. Use this for questions ABOUT a father instead of about a verse: 'what did Chrysostom write on?', 'which books of the Bible did Augustine comment on?', 'what did Jerome say about fasting?', 'who commented on Habakkuk?'. Pass `father` alone for a profile plus the full list of biblical books they commented on, with counts. Pass `father` AND `topic` to search inside that writer's work. Pass `topic` alone to search all 314 writers at once. Pass `father` AND `book` for their commentary on one book. Pass nothing for the list of writers the corpus carries. Quotes returned are verbatim from the curated DB — quote them directly with attribution and never paraphrase from training. When the writer's name is ambiguous (there are four Gregorys) the tool says so and lists the candidates; ask the user which one rather than picking. Each quote carries its `quote_id`; a long one comes as an excerpt (`excerpt` names its parts), and `quote_id` alone returns a quote whole, from any tool that gave the id. The same writer's identical text filed under several verses comes once, the others in `also_under`.

book.description: Optional. Bible book name to scope to, e.g. "Romans". Ignored when `topic` is given.

father.description: Writer name. Loose matching: "augustine", "st augustine" and "Augustine of Hippo" all resolve.

from_part.description: Optional, with quote_id: the part to start from, for a quote returned in parts.

quote_id.description: Optional. A `quote_id` from get_church_fathers or search_fathers: returns that quote whole (past 16,000 characters in parts, with `next_part`). The other parameters are ignored.

topic.description: Optional. Keywords to search for within the commentary text.

name: search_fathers
title: Search the church fathers
